newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures lower, November expiry passes calmly.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures lower, November expiry passes calmly.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice ended lower, dragged down by a spot November contract which fell almost five cents before expiry at noon.
Concern regarding an orderly expiry of November faded as traders were reassured by 700 exchange for physicals.

"That's going to knock quite a chunk off the open interest," said Bernard Savaiko of PaineWebber. "I would say there was a perception there would be adequate deliveries to meet the outstanding open interest."
Open interest in the November contract at close of trade Friday was 2,509 lots.
November juice settled at 107.30 cents per pound, off 4.95 cents. January juice went out 1.70 cents weaker at 97.65 cents per pound.
Traders and analysts said the strong November to January premium helped to prop up the forward months before it expired Friday.
"I think we can see January three cents lower," Savaiko said.
Merrill Lynch said in its weekly Citrus letter that lower prices should help stimulate demand and ultimately drive the market higher.
Merrill added. "One concern is that the trend towards increased usage of chilled juice could be halted this year, leaving more product for processing into FCOJ."
"However, sources indicate that introduction of a new product line of a concentrate based juice and heavy promotions might be the cause for this outlook rather than a slowing demand."
